banner.t: A golden moon with the planets around it; the kettle-drums Nanda and Upananda tied to it

life: Born to Kunti by Dharma; raised in the forest until Pandu’s death
Survives the house of lac; shares Draupadi with his brothers
Performs the Rajasuya and is crowned emperor at Indraprastha
Gambles away his kingdom, his brothers, himself and Draupadi
Answers the Yaksha at the lake and wins back his brothers’ lives
Lives a year in Virata’s court as the dice-master Kanka
Tells Drona the half-truth “Ashwatthama is dead”
Kills Shalya with a spear on the last day of the war
Crowned at Hastinapura; learns the duties of kings from Bhishma
Walks to the Himalayas; reaches heaven in his own body

banner.t: A gigantic silver lion with eyes of lapis lazuli

arms.t: A great mace from the lake Bindu, given by the asura Maya

life: Born to Kunti by Vayu; poisoned and thrown into the river by Duryodhana, he returns stronger
Kills Hidimba and Baka; marries Hidimbi
Kills Jarasandha in a wrestling match; vows to drink Duhshasana’s blood and break Duryodhana’s thigh
Meets his brother Hanuman while fetching flowers for Draupadi
Cook Ballava in Virata’s court; kills Kichaka
Drinks Duhshasana’s blood on the seventeenth day
Breaks Duryodhana’s thighs in the mace duel
Falls on the final journey

banner.t: An ape — Hanuman — of fierce face and lion-like tail

conch.t: Devadatta, from Varuna, found in the lake Bindu

bow.t: Gandiva — made by Brahma, given by Varuna through Agni at Khandava, with two inexhaustible quivers

arms.t: The Pashupata weapon, from Shiva himself

life: Born to Kunti by Indra; Drona’s finest pupil
Wins Draupadi at her svayamvara
Exile of twelve months; marries Ulupi, Chitrangada and Subhadra; burns the Khandava forest
Fights Shiva disguised as a hunter; studies weapons in Indra’s heaven
Lives as the dancer Brihannala; defeats the whole Kaurava host alone
Hears the Bhagavad Gita from Krishna before the battle
Brings down Bhishma from behind Shikhandi
Kills Jayadratha before sunset to avenge Abhimanyu
Kills Karna
Guards the horse of the Ashvamedha; killed by Babhruvahana and revived by Ulupi
Cannot protect the Yadava women; his strength fails

banner.t: A sharabha with a back of gold

life: Born to Madri by the Ashvins
Keeps Virata’s horses as Granthika
Falls on the final journey, for pride in his beauty
Born to Madri by the Ashvins
Vows to kill Shakuni
Keeps Virata’s cattle as Tantipala
Kills Shakuni on the last day
The first of the brothers to fall on the final journey
Born from Drupada’s sacrificial fire
Won by Arjuna; marries all five brothers
Dragged into the dice hall; her honour saved; she wins back her husbands’ freedom
Jayadratha tries to carry her off
Serves Sudeshna as the maid Sairandhri; Kichaka is killed for her
Her five sons are killed in the night raid
The first to fall on the final journey

bow.t: Raudra, the bow Balarama gave him

life: Marries Virata’s daughter Uttara
Breaks into the Chakravyuha on the thirteenth day and is killed inside it
Born to Hidimbi; promises to come whenever his father calls
Wrecks the Kaurava army in the night battle; killed by Karna’s Shakti

banner.t: Made of the trunk of a lofty kovidara tree

life: Born from the fire, in armour, to kill Drona
Made commander of the Pandava army
Beheads Drona
Strangled by Ashwatthama in his sleep

arms.t: The discus Sudarshana from Agni and the mace Kaumodaki from Varuna, given at Khandava

life: Born to Devaki in Kamsa’s prison; raised by Nanda and Yashoda
Has Jarasandha killed; given the first honour at the Rajasuya; kills Shishupala
Goes to Hastinapura as the Pandavas’ envoy; shows his universal form
Speaks the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna
Cursed by Gandhari to see his own clan destroyed
Killed by the hunter Jara after the Yadavas destroy one another
Fights his way to Arjuna on the fourteenth day; beheads Bhurishravas
Killed in the brawl at Prabhasa
Shelters the Pandavas in disguise for their thirteenth year
Killed by Drona on the fifteenth day
Insults his childhood friend Drona; defeated by Drona’s students and loses half his kingdom
Holds the sacrifice from which Draupadi and Dhrishtadyumna are born
Killed by Drona on the fifteenth day
Born a daughter and becomes a man by exchanging sex with a yaksha
Rides before Arjuna against Bhishma on the tenth day
Killed by Ashwatthama in the night raid
Killed by the rakshasa Alambusha on the eighth day

banner.t: A golden palmyra tree with five stars, on a silver standard

life: Born to Ganga; swears never to marry or rule
Carries off the princesses of Kashi for Vichitravirya
Fights Parashurama, his own teacher, to a standstill over Amba
Commands the Kauravas for ten days; tells the Pandavas how he can be beaten
Falls to Arjuna’s arrows on the tenth day
From the bed of arrows, teaches Yudhishthira the duties of kings
Dies at the winter solstice

banner.t: A black deer-skin above a beautiful water-pot

life: Born from a vessel; spurned by Drupada
Teaches the Kuru princes; asks Ekalavya for his thumb
Takes half of Drupada’s kingdom as his fee
Commands the Kauravas after Bhishma; forms the Chakravyuha
Lays down his weapons at “Ashwatthama is dead”; beheaded by Dhrishtadyumna

bow.t: Vijaya, the bow of Indra, from Parashurama

arms.t: Indra’s Shakti, which could kill one foe; spent on Ghatotkacha

life: Born to Kunti by Surya with armour and earrings; set adrift and raised by Adhiratha and Radha
Challenges Arjuna at the tournament; made king of Anga by Duryodhana
Gives his armour and earrings to Indra disguised as a brahmin
Learns from Kunti and Krishna that he is the eldest Pandava; stays with Duryodhana
Refuses to fight while Bhishma commands
Kills Ghatotkacha with the Shakti
Commands the Kauravas; killed by Arjuna while freeing his chariot wheel
Releases the Narayana weapon after his father’s death
Massacres the sleeping Pandava camp
Turns the Brahmashira on Uttara’s unborn child; cursed by Krishna
Found as an infant with his twin Kripi and raised by Shantanu
First teacher of the Kuru princes
Keeps watch at the gate during the night raid
Survives; becomes Parikshit’s teacher

banner.t: A golden ploughshare — the goddess of the furrow

life: Tricked onto the Kaurava side by Duryodhana’s hospitality; promises Yudhishthira to weaken Karna
Drives Karna’s chariot and mocks him
Commands the Kauravas on the last day; killed by Yudhishthira

banner.t: A silver boar on golden chains

life: Tries to carry off Draupadi; shaved and humiliated by Bhima
Wins Shiva’s boon of one day against the Pandavas
Holds the Pandavas back while Abhimanyu dies
Beheaded by Arjuna at sunset on the fourteenth day
His arm cut off by Arjuna as he is about to kill Satyaki; beheaded by Satyaki
Poisons Bhima; plots the house of lac
Humiliated at Indraprastha’s hall of illusions; plans the dice game
Refuses the Pandavas even five villages
Hides in a lake; his thighs broken by Bhima
Dies on hearing of the night raid
Drags Draupadi into the dice hall and tries to strip her
Killed by Bhima, who drinks his blood
Alone among the Kauravas, protests the treatment of Draupadi
Killed by Bhima, who grieves for him
Wins the dice game for Duryodhana
Killed by Sahadeva on the last day
Hurls the Vaishnava weapon at Arjuna; Krishna takes it on his chest
Killed by Arjuna on the twelfth day
Joins Ashwatthama’s night raid
Beheaded by Satyaki at Prabhasa
Raids Virata’s cattle
Leads the Samshaptakas sworn to kill Arjuna
Killed by Arjuna

banner.t: A golden peacock, adorned with jewels

life: Killed by Arjuna on the seventeenth day as Karna watches
Crosses over to the Pandavas before the battle
Left to guard the kingdom when the Pandavas depart
Refuses to take sides; leaves on pilgrimage
Returns for the mace duel and rages at Bhima’s foul blow
Leaves his body in meditation by the sea
Warns the Pandavas of the house of lac
Speaks against the dice game
Shelters Krishna in his house
Dies in the forest; his spirit enters Yudhishthira
Born blind; passed over for the throne
Allows the dice game
Sends Sanjaya to the Pandavas
Crushes an iron statue of Bhima in his grief
Dies in a forest fire with Gandhari and Kunti
Blindfolds herself for life on marrying Dhritarashtra
Gives birth to a mass of flesh that becomes the hundred
Curses Krishna’s clan to destruction
Dies in a forest fire
Given Durvasa’s mantra; bears Karna and sets him adrift
Bears Yudhishthira, Bhima and Arjuna by the gods
Reveals herself to Karna; wins his promise to spare four of her sons
Tells the Pandavas that Karna was their brother
Dies in a forest fire
Fathers Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura by niyoga
Gives Sanjaya divine sight
Shows the widows their dead husbands for one night
Carries Dhritarashtra’s message to the Pandavas
Narrates the war, and the Gita, to the blind king
Clears the earth of kshatriyas twenty-one times
Fights Bhishma for Amba
Curses Karna for hiding his birth
